title: Backward sweep without leftward growth
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet and let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$ with $k$ work tapes. Choose $a_0\in\Gamma$, a state $q$, an optional input symbol, work-tape reads, and Boolean right-head flags. Suppose there is no tape whose right-head flag is true and whose prescribed head movement is left. For any input-head position, output word, integer $z$, and left stack $l$, the augmented simulator, starting in the backward-writing phase with the boundary marker on its right, reaches after one step the left-growth phase with the action's optional successor state, unchanged frontier $z$, unchanged left stack $l$, and the boundary marker still on its right; throughout this step its work-tape head remains at $z$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
A Boolean right-head flag for each tape
No tape flagged on the right has a prescribed leftward move
An input-head position, output word, integer $z$, and left stack $l$
